sanskrit: jahi saubhaṃ svavīryeṇa ye cātra ripavo mama ity uktvā bhujavīryeṇa tasmai prāhiṇavaṃ ruṣā
english: "Destroy Saubha by your own valour, and also the enemies of mine who are here." Saying this, in anger I hurled it at him with the strength of my arms.

sanskrit: rūpaṃ sudarśanasyāsīd ākāśe patatas tadā dvitīyasyeva sūryasya yugānte pariviṣyataḥ
english: The form of Sudarshana as it flew through the sky was then like a second sun blazing at the end of an age.

sanskrit: tat samāsādya nagaraṃ saubhaṃ vyapagatatviṣam madhyena pāṭayām āsa krakaco dārv ivocchritam
english: Reaching that city Saubha and stripping it of its lustre, it split it down the middle as a saw splits a tall piece of timber.

sanskrit: dvidhā kṛtaṃ tataḥ saubhaṃ sudarśanabalād dhatam maheśvaraśaroddhūtaṃ papāta tripuraṃ yathā
english: Saubha was thus cleft in two and struck down by the power of Sudarshana; it fell as Tripura fell when shattered by the arrow of Maheshvara.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite saubhe cakram āgāt karaṃ mama punaś coddhūya vegena śālvāyety aham abruvam
english: When Saubha had fallen, the discus returned to my hand; lifting it again with speed, I cried out: "Now for Shalva!"

sanskrit: tataḥ śālvaṃ gadāṃ gurvīm āvidhyantaṃ mahāhave dvidhā cakāra sahasā prajajvāla ca tejasā
english: Then Shalva, who was swinging his massive mace in that great battle, was suddenly cut in two, and the discus blazed with radiance.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite vīre dānavās trastacetasaḥ hāhābhūtā diśo jagmur arditā mama sāyakaiḥ
english: When that hero fell, the Danavas, terror-stricken in their hearts, fled crying "Alas!" in all directions, tormented by my arrows.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ samavasthāpya rathaṃ saubhasamīpataḥ śaṅkhaṃ pradhmāpya harṣeṇa suhṛdaḥ paryaharṣayam
english: Then, having positioned my chariot near where Saubha had fallen, I blew my conch with joy and filled my friends with delight.

sanskrit: tan meruśikharākāraṃ vidhvastāṭṭālagopuram dahyamānam abhiprekṣya striyas tāḥ saṃpradudruvuḥ
english: Seeing that city, shaped like the peak of Meru, with its battlements and gatehouses shattered, burning fiercely, the women fled in all directions.

sanskrit: evaṃ nihatya samare śālvaṃ saubhaṃ nipātya ca ānartān punar āgamya suhṛdāṃ prītim āvaham
english: Having thus slain Shalva in battle and brought down Saubha, I returned again to the Anarta land and brought joy to my friends.

sanskrit: etasmāt kāraṇād rājan nāgamaṃ nāgasāhvayam yady agāṃ paravīraghna na hi jīvet suyodhanaḥ
english: It is for this reason, O king, that I did not come to the city named after the elephant; had I gone there, O slayer of enemy heroes, Suyodhana would not be alive today.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā mahābāhuḥ kauravaṃ puruṣottamaḥ āmantrya prayayau dhīmān pāṇḍavān madhusūdanaḥ
english: Vaishampāyana said: Having spoken thus, the mighty-armed best of men, Madhusudana, the wise one, took leave of the Kauravas and the Pandavas and departed.

sanskrit: abhivādya mahābāhur dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram rājñā mūrdhany upāghrāto bhīmena ca mahābhujaḥ
english: The mighty-armed one paid his respects to Dharmaraja Yudhishthira and was smelled on the crown of the head by the king, and likewise by Bhima of great arms.

sanskrit: subhadrām abhimanyuṃ ca ratham āropya kāñcanam āruroha rathaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ pāṇḍavair abhipūjitaḥ
english: Krishna, honoured by the Pandavas, placed Subhadra and Abhimanyu upon the golden chariot, then mounted it himself.

sanskrit: sainyasugrīvayuktena rathenādityavarcasā dvārakāṃ prayayau kṛṣṇaḥ samāśvāsya yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Krishna departed for Dvaraka on a chariot yoked with Sainya and Sugriva, blazing like the sun, having first consoled Yudhishthira.

sanskrit: tataḥ prayāte dāśārhe dhṛṣṭadyumno 'pi pārṣataḥ draupadeyān upādāya prayayau svapuraṃ tadā
english: Then, after the descendant of the Dasharhas had departed, Dhrishtadyumna, son of Prishata, also took the sons of Draupadi and went to his own city.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭaketuḥ svasāraṃ ca samādāyātha cedirāṭ jagāma pāṇḍavān dṛṣṭvā ramyāṃ śuktimatīṃ purīm
english: Dhrishtaketu, king of the Chedis, also took his sister and, having bidden farewell to the Pandavas, departed for the lovely city of Shuktimatī.

sanskrit: kekayāś cāpy anujñātāḥ kaunteyenāmitaujasā āmantrya pāṇḍavān sarvān prayayus te 'pi bhārata
english: The Kekayas too, permitted to leave by Kuntī's son of immeasurable might, took their leave of all the Pandavas and also departed, O Bharata.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāś ca viśaś caiva tathā viṣayavāsinaḥ visṛjyamānāḥ subhṛśaṃ na tyajanti sma pāṇḍavān
english: The brahmanas, the Vaishyas, and the inhabitants of the provinces, though being dismissed, would not abandon the Pandavas.

sanskrit: samavāyaḥ sa rājendra sumahādbhutadarśanaḥ āsīn mahātmanāṃ teṣāṃ kāmyake bharatarṣabha
english: That assembly of great souls in Kamyaka was a wondrous spectacle to behold, O lord of kings, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu viprāṃs tān anumānya mahāmanāḥ śaśāsa puruṣān kāle rathān yojayateti ha
english: But Yudhishthira, great-souled, having honoured those brahmanas, in due time ordered his men: "Yoke the chariots."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasmin daśārhādhipatau prayāte; yudhiṣṭhiro bhīmasenārjunau ca yamau ca kṛṣṇā ca purohitaś ca; rathān mahārhān paramāśvayuktān
english: Vaishampāyana said: When the lord of the Dasharhas had departed, Yudhishthira, Bhimasena, Arjuna, the twins, Krishnā, and the family priest mounted their excellent chariots yoked with the finest horses.

sanskrit: āsthāya vīrāḥ sahitā vanāya; pratasthire bhūtapatiprakāśāḥ hiraṇyaniṣkān vasanāni gāś ca; pradāya śikṣākṣaramantravidbhyaḥ
english: Those heroes, united, resplendent as lords of beings, set out together for the forest, having first given golden nishkas, garments, and cows to those versed in the teaching of sacred syllables and mantras.

sanskrit: preṣyāḥ puro viṃśatir āttaśastrā; dhanūṃṣi varmāṇi śarāṃś ca pītān maurvīś ca yantrāṇi ca sāyakāṃś ca; sarve samādāya jaghanyam īyuḥ
english: Twenty armed retainers went ahead; and all of them, carrying bows, armour, yellow-tinted arrows, bowstrings, mechanical devices, and quivers, marched in the rear.

sanskrit: tatas tu vāsāṃsi ca rājaputryā; dhātryaś ca dāsyaś ca vibhūṣaṇaṃ ca tad indrasenas tvaritaṃ pragṛhya; jaghanyam evopayayau rathena
english: Then Indrasena, swiftly taking up the princess's garments, her nurses, her maidservants, and her ornaments, followed in the rear with his chariot.

sanskrit: tataḥ kuruśreṣṭham upetya paurāḥ; pradakṣiṇaṃ cakrur adīnasattvāḥ taṃ brāhmaṇāś cābhyavadan prasannā; mukhyāś ca sarve kurujāṅgalānām
english: Then the citizens, undaunted in spirit, approached the foremost of the Kurus and circumambulated him; the brahmanas greeted him warmly, as did all the leading men of the Kurujangala region.

sanskrit: sa cāpi tān abhyavadat prasannaḥ; sahaiva tair bhrātṛbhir dharmarājaḥ tasthau ca tatrādhipatir mahātmā; dṛṣṭvā janaughaṃ kurujāṅgalānām
english: He in turn greeted them with kindness — Dharmaraja along with his brothers — and that great-souled lord stood there, gazing at the throng of people from Kurujangala.

sanskrit: piteva putreṣu sa teṣu bhāvaṃ; cakre kurūṇām ṛṣabho mahātmā te cāpi tasmin bharataprabarhe; tadā babhūvuḥ pitarīva putrāḥ
english: The great-souled bull of the Kurus felt toward them as a father feels toward his sons; and they in turn, toward that foremost of the Bharatas, were then as sons toward a father.

sanskrit: tataḥ samāsādya mahājanaughāḥ; kurupravīraṃ parivārya tasthuḥ hā nātha hā dharma iti bruvanto; hriyā ca sarve 'śrumukhā babhūvuḥ
english: Then the great multitude of people, approaching the foremost hero of the Kurus, stood surrounding him, crying "Alas, our lord! Alas, O Dharma!" — and all with tear-streaked faces from grief.

sanskrit: varaḥ kurūṇām adhipaḥ prajānāṃ; piteva putrān apahāya cāsmān paurān imāñ jānapadāṃś ca sarvān; hitvā prayātaḥ kva nu dharmarājaḥ
english: "Where has Dharmaraja gone, the best of the Kurus, the lord of his people, who, like a father abandoning his sons, has left us — these citizens and all the country folk?"

sanskrit: dhig dhārtarāṣṭraṃ sunṛśaṃsabuddhiṃ; sasaubalaṃ pāpamatiṃ ca karṇam anartham icchanti narendra pāpā; ye dharmanityasya satas tavogrāḥ
english: "Shame on the son of Dhritarashtra, so cruel of mind, on Saubala, and on Karna of evil intent — those sinners who desire your misfortune, O lord of men, you who are ever steadfast in righteousness."

sanskrit: svayaṃ niveśyāpratimaṃ mahātmā; puraṃ mahad devapuraprakāśam śatakratuprastham amoghakarmā; hitvā prayātaḥ kva nu dharmarājaḥ
english: "Where has Dharmaraja gone, the great-souled one of unfailing deeds, who himself built that matchless great city, shining like the city of the gods, the city of Shatakratu, and then abandoned it?"

sanskrit: cakāra yām apratimāṃ mahātmā; sabhāṃ mayo devasabhāprakāśām tāṃ devaguptām iva devamāyāṃ; hitvā prayātaḥ kva nu dharmarājaḥ
english: "Where has Dharmaraja gone, abandoning that incomparable assembly hall which Maya built for the great-souled one, bright as the hall of the gods, guarded by the gods like some divine illusion?"

sanskrit: tān dharmakāmārthavid uttamaujā; bībhatsur uccaiḥ sahitān uvāca ādāsyate vāsam imaṃ niruṣya; vaneṣu rājā dviṣatāṃ yaśāṃsi
english: Bibhatsu, of supreme valour and versed in dharma, pleasure, and artha, spoke to them all with a loud voice: "Having completed this sojourn in the forests, the king will strip his enemies of their glory."

sanskrit: dvijātimukhyāḥ sahitāḥ pṛthak ca; bhavadbhir āsādya tapasvinaś ca prasādya dharmārthavidaś ca vācyā; yathārthasiddhiḥ paramā bhaven naḥ
english: "O foremost among the twice-born, you should go separately or together, approach the ascetics, propitiate those versed in dharma and artha, and speak so that our highest goal may be accomplished."

sanskrit: ity evam ukte vacane 'rjunena; te brāhmaṇāḥ sarvavarṇāś ca rājan mudābhyanandan sahitāś ca cakruḥ; pradakṣiṇaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭham
english: When Arjuna had spoken these words, O king, those brahmanas and people of all castes rejoiced together and circumambulated the foremost upholder of dharma.

sanskrit: āmantrya pārthaṃ ca vṛkodaraṃ ca; dhanaṃjayaṃ yājñasenīṃ yamau ca pratasthire rāṣṭram apetaharṣā; yudhiṣṭhireṇānumatā yathāsvam
english: Taking leave of Partha, Vrikodara, Dhananjaya, Yajnaseni, and the twins, and with Yudhishthira's permission, they departed for their respective homelands, their joy departed.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas teṣu prayāteṣu kaunteyaḥ satyasaṃgaraḥ abhyabhāṣata dharmātmā bhrātṝn sarvān yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Vaishampāyana said: Then, when they had departed, Yudhishthira, son of Kuntī, true to his vows, virtuous of soul, addressed all his brothers.

sanskrit: dvādaśemāḥ samāsmābhir vastavyaṃ nirjane vane samīkṣadhvaṃ mahāraṇye deśaṃ bahumṛgadvijam
english: "We must dwell in the lonely forest for these twelve years. Choose a region in the great wilderness that abounds in deer and birds."

sanskrit: bahupuṣpaphalaṃ ramyaṃ śivaṃ puṇyajanocitam yatremāḥ śaradaḥ sarvāḥ sukhaṃ prativasemahi
english: "Rich in flowers and fruits, beautiful, auspicious, fit for holy people — a place where we may dwell comfortably through all these years."

sanskrit: evam ukte pratyuvāca dharmarājaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ guruvan mānavaguruṃ mānayitvā manasvinam
english: When he had spoken thus, Dhananjaya replied to Dharmaraja, honouring that guide of men as one honours a guru, respecting his noble spirit.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca bhavān eva maharṣīṇāṃ vṛddhānāṃ paryupāsitā ajñātaṃ mānuṣe loke bhavato nāsti kiṃ cana
english: Arjuna said: You are yourself the attendant of the great sages and elders; there is nothing in the world of men that is unknown to you.

sanskrit: tvayā hy upāsitā nityaṃ brāhmaṇā bharatarṣabha dvaipāyanaprabhṛtayo nāradaś ca mahātapāḥ
english: For you have always served the brahmanas, O bull of the Bharatas — Dvaipayana and the rest, and the great ascetic Narada.

sanskrit: yaḥ sarvalokadvārāṇi nityaṃ saṃcarate vaśī devalokād brahmalokaṃ gandharvāpsarasām api
english: He who always travels self-controlled through the gates of all worlds — from the world of the gods to the world of Brahma, and even to the realm of the Gandharvas and Apsaras.

sanskrit: sarvā gatīr vijānāsi brāhmaṇānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ prabhāvāṃś caiva vettha tvaṃ sarveṣām eva pārthiva
english: You know all the paths of the brahmanas — there is no doubt. And you know the powers of all of them, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: tvam eva rājañ jānāsi śreyaḥkāraṇam eva ca yatrecchasi mahārāja nivāsaṃ tatra kurmahe
english: You alone, O king, know what is truly beneficial. Wherever you wish to dwell, O great king, there shall we go.

sanskrit: idaṃ dvaitavanaṃ nāma saraḥ puṇyajanocitam bahupuṣpaphalaṃ ramyaṃ nānādvijaniṣevitam
english: This lake called Dvaitavana is fit for holy people, rich in flowers and fruits, beautiful, and frequented by various birds.

sanskrit: atremā dvādaśa samā viharemeti rocaye yadi te 'numataṃ rājan kiṃ vānyan manyate bhavān
english: "It pleases me that we spend these twelve years here — if it meets with your approval, O king, or what else does Your Honour think?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca mamāpy etan mataṃ pārtha tvayā yat samudāhṛtam gacchāma puṇyaṃ vikhyātaṃ mahad dvaitavanaṃ saraḥ
english: Yudhishthira said: This is my view too, O Partha, what you have proposed. Let us go to the great and renowned lake of Dvaitavana, a holy place.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas te prayayuḥ sarve pāṇḍavā dharmacāriṇaḥ brāhmaṇair bahubhiḥ sārdhaṃ puṇyaṃ dvaitavanaṃ saraḥ
english: Vaishampāyana said: Then all the Pandavas, those walkers of the path of dharma, set out together with many brahmanas for the holy lake of Dvaitavana.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ sāgnihotrāś ca tathaiva ca niragnayaḥ svādhyāyino bhikṣavaś ca sajapā vanavāsinaḥ
english: Brahmanas who maintained the agnihotra fire, and those who did not; those devoted to recitation, wandering ascetics, those given to silent repetition, and forest dwellers —

sanskrit: bahavo brāhmaṇās tatra parivavrur yudhiṣṭhiram tapasvinaḥ satyaśīlāḥ śataśaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ
english: — many brahmanas, ascetics of truthful nature and firm vows, by the hundreds surrounded Yudhishthira there.

sanskrit: te yātvā pāṇḍavās tatra bahubhir brāhmaṇaiḥ saha puṇyaṃ dvaitavanaṃ ramyaṃ viviśur bharatarṣabhāḥ
english: The Pandavas, those bulls of the Bharatas, went there and entered the holy, beautiful Dvaitavana together with many brahmanas.

sanskrit: tac chālatālāmramadhūkanīpa; kadambasarjārjunakarṇikāraiḥ tapātyaye puṣpadharaiḥ upetaṃ; mahāvanaṃ rāṣṭrapatir dadarśa
english: The lord of the kingdom beheld that great forest filled at the end of the hot season with flowering shāla, palm, mango, madhūka, nīpa, kadamba, sarjā, arjuna, and karnikāra trees.

sanskrit: mahādrumāṇāṃ śikhareṣu tasthur; manoramāṃ vācam udīrayantaḥ mayūradātyūhacakorasaṃghās; tasmin vane kānanakokilāś ca
english: Perched on the tops of the great trees, uttering their charming calls, were flocks of peacocks, dātyūha birds, chakoras, and forest cuckoos throughout that woodland.

sanskrit: kareṇuyūthaiḥ saha yūthapānāṃ; madotkaṭānām acalaprabhāṇām mahānti yūthāni mahādvipānāṃ; tasmin vane rāṣṭrapatir dadarśa
english: The lord of the kingdom beheld in that forest great herds of mighty elephants, steady as mountains, intoxicated with rut, together with their female consorts and the bull leaders of the herds.

sanskrit: manoramāṃ bhogavatīm upetya; dhṛtātmanāṃ cīrajaṭādharāṇām tasmin vane dharmabhṛtāṃ nivāse; dadarśa siddharṣigaṇān anekān
english: Approaching that lovely and prosperous land, in that forest which was the abode of the upholders of dharma, he saw many groups of siddhas and sages, wearing bark garments and matted locks, firm in spirit.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa yānād avaruhya rājā; sabhrātṛkaḥ sajanaḥ kānanaṃ tat viveśa dharmātmavatāṃ variṣṭhas; triviṣṭapaṃ śakra ivāmitaujāḥ
english: Then that king, the foremost among the virtuous of soul, descended from his vehicle and, together with his brothers and retinue, entered that forest like Shakra of immeasurable might entering the third heaven.

sanskrit: taṃ satyasaṃdhaṃ sahitābhipetur; didṛkṣavaś cāraṇasiddhasaṃghāḥ vanaukasaś cāpi narendrasiṃhaṃ; manasvinaṃ saṃparivārya tasthuḥ
english: Eager to behold him, that keeper of his word, groups of Charanas and Siddhas converged upon him; and the forest-dwellers too stood surrounding that lion among kings, that noble-spirited one.

sanskrit: sa tatra siddhān abhivādya sarvān; pratyarcito rājavad devavac ca viveśa sarvaiḥ sahito dvijāgryaiḥ; kṛtāñjalir dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhaḥ
english: He there paid his respects to all the Siddhas; honoured in return as befits a king and as befits a god, the foremost upholder of dharma, his palms joined, entered together with all the leading twice-born.

sanskrit: sa puṇyaśīlaḥ pitṛvan mahātmā; tapasvibhir dharmaparair upetya pratyarcitaḥ puṣpadharasya mūle; mahādrumasyopaviveśa rājā
english: That virtuous, great-souled king, fatherly in nature, was approached by ascetics devoted to dharma, and honoured by them, sat down at the foot of a great tree laden with flowers.

sanskrit: bhīmaś ca kṛṣṇā ca dhanaṃjayaś ca; yamau ca te cānucarā narendram vimucya vāhān avaruhya sarve; tatropatasthur bharataprabarhāḥ
english: Bhima, Krishnā, Dhananjaya, the twins, and their attendants — those foremost of the Bharatas — all dismounted from their conveyances, freed the horses, and stood in attendance upon the lord of men there.

sanskrit: latāvatānāvanataḥ sa pāṇḍavair; mahādrumaḥ pañcabhir ugradhanvibhiḥ babhau nivāsopagatair mahātmabhir; mahāgirir vāraṇayūthapair iva
english: That great tree, bent low with canopies of vines, graced by those five mighty-bowed great-souled Pandavas who had come to dwell beneath it, shone like a great mountain surrounded by elephant herd-lords.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tat kānanaṃ prāpya narendraputrāḥ; sukhocitā vāsam upetya kṛcchram vijahrur indrapratimāḥ śiveṣu; sarasvatīśālavaneṣu teṣu
english: Vaishampāyana said: Having reached that forest, those sons of the lord of men, accustomed to comfort, having come to their arduous dwelling, sported like images of Indra in those auspicious groves of Sarasvati and shāla trees.

sanskrit: yatīṃś ca sarvān sa munīṃś ca rājā; tasmin vane mūlaphalair udagraiḥ dvijātimukhyān ṛṣabhaḥ kurūṇāṃ; saṃtarpayām āsa mahānubhāvaḥ
english: The great-souled bull of the Kurus, that king, gratified all the renouncers and sages in that forest, and the foremost among the twice-born, with abundant roots and fruits.

sanskrit: iṣṭīś ca pitryāṇi tathāgriyāṇi; mahāvane vasatāṃ pāṇḍavānām purohitaḥ sarvasamṛddhatejāś; cakāra dhaumyaḥ pitṛvat kurūṇām
english: The family priest Dhaumya, of full and brilliant splendour, performed the ancestral and the first-offering sacrificial rites for the Pandavas dwelling in the great forest, treating the Kurus as a father would.

sanskrit: apetya rāṣṭrād vasatāṃ tu teṣām; ṛṣiḥ purāṇo 'tithir ājagāma tam āśramaṃ tīvrasamṛddhatejā; mārkaṇḍeyaḥ śrīmatāṃ pāṇḍavānām
english: While they were dwelling there having gone from their kingdom, the ancient sage Markandeya, glowing with intense and full radiance, came as a guest to that hermitage of the illustrious Pandavas.

sanskrit: sa sarvavid draupadīṃ prekṣya kṛṣṇāṃ; yudhiṣṭhiraṃ bhīmasenārjunau ca saṃsmṛtya rāmaṃ manasā mahātmā; tapasvimadhye 'smayatāmitaujāḥ
english: That all-knowing, great-souled one of immeasurable might, beholding Draupadi Krishnā, Yudhishthira, Bhimasena, and Arjuna, and then mentally recalling Rama, smiled amid the assembly of ascetics.

sanskrit: taṃ dharmarājo vimanā ivābravīt; sarve hriyā santi tapasvino 'mī bhavān idaṃ kiṃ smayatīva hṛṣṭas; tapasvināṃ paśyatāṃ mām udīkṣya
english: Dharmaraja, as if troubled, spoke to him: "All these ascetics present feel shame — why does Your Honour seem to smile with joy, looking at me as the ascetics watch?"

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca na tāta hṛṣyāmi na ca smayāmi; praharṣajo māṃ bhajate na darpaḥ tavāpadaṃ tv adya samīkṣya rāmaṃ; satyavrataṃ dāśarathiṃ smarāmi
english: Markandeya said: I do not rejoice, dear one, nor do I smile; neither elation nor pride comes upon me. But seeing your misfortune today, I call to mind Rama, the son of Dasharatha, true to his vow.

sanskrit: sa cāpi rājā saha lakṣmaṇena; vane nivāsaṃ pitur eva śāsanāt dhanvī caran pārtha purā mayaiva; dṛṣṭo girer ṛṣyamūkasya sānau
english: That king too, bearing his bow, together with Lakshmana, dwelling in the forest by his father's command, was seen by me long ago, O Partha, on the slopes of mount Rishyamuka.

sanskrit: sahasranetrapratimo mahātmā; mayasya jeta namuceś ca hantā pitur nideśād anaghaḥ svadharmaṃ; vane vāsaṃ dāśarathiś cakāra
english: That great-souled one, equal to Sahasranetra, conqueror of Maya and slayer of Namuchi, the faultless son of Dasharatha, fulfilled his own dharma by dwelling in the forest at his father's command.

sanskrit: sa cāpi śakrasya samaprabhāvo; mahānubhāvaḥ samareṣv ajeyaḥ vihāya bhogān acarad vaneṣu; neśe balasyeti cared adharmam
english: He too, equal in might to Shakra, of great power, unconquerable in battles, gave up his pleasures and roamed through the forests — for one who has the strength should not act unrightously.

sanskrit: nṛpāś ca nābhāgabhagīrathādayo; mahīm imāṃ sāgarāntāṃ vijitya satyena te 'py ajayaṃs tāta lokān; neśe balasyeti cared adharmam
english: And kings such as Nabhaga, Bhagiratha and others, having conquered this earth to its ocean shores, also won the worlds through truth, dear one — for one who has the strength should not act unrighteously.

sanskrit: alarkam āhur naravarya santaṃ; satyavrataṃ kāśikarūṣarājam vihāya rāṣṭrāṇi vasūni caiva; neśe balasyeti cared adharmam
english: They call Alarka, O best of men, a righteous one — the king of the Kashi and Rūsha lands, true to his vow; he renounced his kingdoms and his wealth — for one who has the strength should not act unrighteously.

sanskrit: dhātrā vidhir yo vihitaḥ purāṇas; taṃ pūjayanto naravarya santaḥ saptarṣayaḥ pārtha divi prabhānti; neśe balasyeti cared adharmam
english: Honouring the ancient ordinance ordained by the Creator, O best of men, the seven righteous sages shine in heaven, O Partha — for one who has the strength should not act unrighteously.

sanskrit: mahābalān parvatakūṭamātrān; viṣāṇinaḥ paśya gajān narendra sthitān nideśe naravarya dhātur; neśe balasyeti cared adharmam
english: Behold the elephants, O lord of men, great in strength, as large as mountain peaks, bearing tusks — they stand within the Creator's ordinance, O best of men — for one who has the strength should not act unrighteously.

sanskrit: sarvāṇi bhūtāni narendra paśya; yathā yathāvad vihitaṃ vidhātrā svayonitas tat kurute prabhāvān; neśe balasyeti cared adharmam
english: Behold all beings, O lord of men — each one, however mighty, acts according to what the Creator has ordained from its own nature — for one who has the strength should not act unrighteously.

sanskrit: satyena dharmeṇa yathārhavṛttyā; hriyā tathā sarvabhūtāny atītya yaśaś ca tejaś ca tavāpi dīptaṃ; vibhāvasor bhāskarasyeva pārtha
english: Through truth, through righteousness, through conduct befitting your station, and through modesty, surpassing all beings — your glory and your radiance blaze too, O Partha, like that of the fire and the sun.

sanskrit: yathāpratijñaṃ ca mahānubhāva; kṛcchraṃ vane vāsam imaṃ niruṣya tataḥ śriyaṃ tejasā svena dīptām; ādāsyase pārthiva kauravebhyaḥ
english: And as you have vowed, O great-souled one, having endured this hard dwelling in the forest, you shall then, O lord of the earth, wrest from the Kauravas a sovereignty blazing with your own radiance.
